summary.tpReason: A successful NOERROR DNS lookup for avsvmcloud.com was recorded and explicitly allowed, and this domain is documented by Mandiant as the SUNBURST DNS C2 coordinator. That makes the alert materially suspicious. Confidence is reduced because the event is a single apex-domain lookup (not a DGA subdomain), has no host/process identity, and has no corroborating network or endpoint telemetry.
summary.fpReason: The telemetry proves a DNS lookup, not that SUNBURST or another malicious process issued it. Only one event exists, the source is represented as an IP rather than a host, and no follow-on connection or endpoint detection was found. A test, research, or incidental lookup remains plausible.
summary.whatHappened: At 2020-03-20 16:52:16.153 UTC, Umbrella DNS telemetry recorded source/internal IP 17.81.146.1 querying avsvmcloud.com for an A record through external IP 15.230.137.45. The request was Allowed and returned NOERROR; policy and identity were both HOSTNAME. Sentinel generated the High alert at the same timestamp. The available data does not identify the hostname/process behind 17.81.146.1 or show whether any subsequent C2 connection occurred.
keyEvidence: solarigate_beacon_umbrella_CL contains exactly one matching event: 2020-03-20T16:52:16.153Z, avsvmcloud.com, InternalIp 17.81.146.1, ExternalIp 15.230.137.45, Action Allowed, QueryType 1 (A), ResponseCode NOERROR.
SecurityAlert confirms the same event and entities, with status New, severity High, and no additional connection details.

Mandiant/Google Cloud, “SUNBURST Additional Technical Details” (2020-12-24), https://cloud.google.com/blog/topics/threat-intelligence/sunburst-additional-technical-details — describes avsvmcloud[.]com as the SUNBURST C2 coordinator and its DNS-based beaconing; it also states that follow-on C2 may occur after relevant CNAME resolution.

No matching 17.81.146.1, 15.230.137.45, or avsvmcloud.com events were found in the searched CommonSecurityLog, CrowdStrike detections/hosts, or other available telemetry beyond this DNS event and the alert.
The query is for the apex avsvmcloud.com, not a documented SUNBURST DGA subdomain; therefore the DNS evidence is suspicious but not conclusive of SUNBURST execution.
researchDone: Queried the matching solarigate_beacon_umbrella_CL event and searched the full available telemetry for avsvmcloud.com and both alert IPs.
Reviewed the alert record, extended properties, entities, timestamps, action, query type, and DNS response code.
Checked the 30-minute window around the event for additional Umbrella DNS activity; only one event for 17.81.146.1 was present.
Checked CommonSecurityLog for matching IPs/domain and nearby network activity; no rows returned.
Checked CrowdStrikeDetections and CrowdStrikeHosts for matching IPs; no matching rows returned.
Researched SUNBURST avsvmcloud.com behavior using Mandiant’s Google Cloud technical advisory; it supports C2 relevance but does not establish that this specific lookup was malware-generated.
